sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1971.2 ± 487.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by fluorescently-tagged anti-HA antibody staining (fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry); ligand-induced internalization of the tagged receptor monitored quantitatively — receptor traffics normally in response to S1P.
sites.rationale: S1PR1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–48 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 49, leaving the N-terminus as the only extracellular terminus. No residue number is named in any ledger line, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists, so the position is topology-derived as a prepend (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M). Python confirms residue 1 is M and TM1 is ≥48 residues away, providing ample room for a short epitope tag. The 3xHA tag was confirmed on the cell surface by antibody staining and the receptor underwent normal ligand-induced internalization, satisfying surface_and_function. Full-length S1PR1 with 3xHA fused at its N-terminus (described explicitly as 'in the lumen', i.e. extracellular) and eGFP or mCherry at the C-terminus (3xHA-S1PR1-eGFP and 3xHA-S1PR1-mCherry) expressed in cells. S1PR1 has no signal peptide; the N-terminus (residues 1–48) is the sole extracellular terminus, so the tag prepends before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0). Corroborated by L7/L8 (HA-S1P1, N-terminal HA by SLIC cloning) and L9 (pBiT3.1-N HiBiT at N-terminus used in functional reversibility assays).

sources.claim: The experiments were carried out with cells ectopically expressing S1PR1 fused at its N-terminus at, in the lumen, to a tandem repeat of three hemagglutinin epitope tags (3xHA) and at its C-terminus, in the cytosol, with eGFP or mCherry (3xHA-S1PR1-eGFP and 3xHA-S1PR1-mCherry, respectively).

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines converge on two tag positions: (1) N-terminal extracellular prepend (L1, L2, L7, L8, L9) and (2) C-terminal intracellular GFP fusion (L3, L4, L5, L6). The C-terminal site is intracellular (topology landmarks: residues 313–382 are intracellular) and is therefore recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tag in any of the three short extracellular loops (ECL1: 104–120, ECL2: 181–201, ECL3: 279–294); those loops are not proposed as sites because the ledger provides no qualifying insertion there. L9 names M124 only as a mutation site within TM2 (residues 121–140); the tag itself is at the N-terminus (pBiT3.1-N = N-terminal HiBiT), so M124 is not a tag site. L7/L8 and L9 independently corroborate the N-terminal extracellular site already grounded in L1, so only one site is reported (not duplicated per ledger line).

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion (PC12-S1PR1-GFP, HEK293-S1PR1-GFP) confirmed at plasma membrane by confocal imaging, but the C-terminus (residues 313–382) is intracellular per topology landmarks — suitable for cytoplasmic labelling or a snorkel construct, not for extracellular surface tagging.
